chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 461: The Evil Spirits - Bai Lingmiao Mutates!
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang faces a village overrun by evil spirits during the Heavenly Calamity. He finds Bai Lingmiao transformed into a monstrous, laughing beast and uses a terrifying ritual to stop her.
og_title: The Evil Spirits - A Face is Removed | Dao Gui Yi Xian
og_description: The Calamity brings a flood of evil spirits. In her room, Bai Lingmiao is no longer human—she is a laughing, devouring monster. Li Huowang performs a desperate, intimate ritual.
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 461: Bai Lingmiao Goes Feral
twitter_description: Evil spirits fill the village. Li Huowang finds Bai Lingmiao mutated and laughing, and must use a face-removing ritual to try and save her.

lore_anchors.definition: A generic term in Chinese folk religion for a malignant, unclean spirit, often born from violent death or resentment.
A yellow, mineral-dyed paper used in Daoist talisman-writing, believed to have protective and warding properties against evil.
The Chinese mythological capital of the underworld, a city of the dead ruled by the God of the Earth's Prison.
The silent, often possessed assistant in a chuma ritual; here, Bai Lingmiao's own Second Spirit is also corrupted.
The special domino tile Li Huowang uses for his ritual; a tool he has previously used for cultivation, here repurposed for a face-removal technique.
A phrase referencing a Daoist meditative practice of cutting off worldly ties and focusing the mind; here literalized into a ritual action.
A phrase from the Daoist text *Zhuangzi*, referring to a state of profound tranquility leading to enlightenment; here used as a command to stabilize Bai Lingmiao.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is a "Heavenly Calamity" in this context?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is an ontological disaster where a fundamental law of reality breaks down; in this case, the sky has gone permanently dark, and the barrier between worlds is thinning, allowing evil spirits to proliferate.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Bai Lingmiao laughing while she is transformed?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The "Immortals" (the spirits possessing her in her role as a chuma medium) are overjoyed by the chaos of the Calamity, and their overwhelming ecstasy is leaking into her consciousness, forcing her to laugh involuntarily.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How did Li Huowang "remove his face"?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Using a cell-based technique, he pressed a domino tile to his forehead and used a hand seal to detach his own skin like a mask, which he then pressed onto Bai Lingmiao to impose his state of calm over her corrupted one. It is a literal, not metaphorical, ritual act.
